questions.q: What is usually the deciding factor between choosing a Lakehouse and a Warehouse?
options: Who's actually querying the data day to day — a PySpark-fluent team or a T-SQL-fluent team
Which one is cheaper regardless of team skillset
Lakehouses are always the objectively superior choice
Warehouses cannot store any data, only Lakehouses can
questions.explain: A team fluent in T-SQL gets real value from a Warehouse's native INSERT/UPDATE support that a Lakehouse's read-only endpoint can't offer.

questions.q: Is it valid for a real organization to use both a Lakehouse and a Warehouse in the same project?
options: Yes — a common mixed pattern is bronze/silver in a Lakehouse (PySpark cleaning) feeding a Warehouse's gold layer (T-SQL aggregation)
No, a single project must use exactly one item type throughout
Only if the Lakehouse and Warehouse are in different workspaces
Mixed patterns are technically possible but never actually used
questions.explain: This is genuinely the same medallion shape from Databricks & Delta Lake's Chapter 3, just split across two item types.

questions.q: Why does this course's own NYC Taxi pipeline use a Lakehouse rather than a Warehouse?
options: Its cleaning logic is PySpark — the same DataFrame methods from Foundations' Chapter 4 — with no separate analyst team needing native T-SQL writes
Warehouses cannot store NYC Taxi data at all
Lakehouses are always required for any real-time data
This course never explains its reasoning for this choice
questions.explain: A Warehouse would be the wrong default choice for this specific pipeline, even though it's correct for many other real gold layers.

questions.q: How does the Lakehouse-vs-Warehouse decision compare to Databricks & Delta Lake's all-purpose vs. job cluster distinction?
options: Both are real, meaningful choices between two genuinely different tools, not two skins on the same underlying thing
There's no meaningful comparison between the two decisions
All-purpose and job clusters are actually the same as Lakehouse and Warehouse, just renamed
The cluster decision was purely cosmetic, unlike this one
questions.explain: This reinforces that choosing between the two Fabric item types is a real decision, not a formality.

questions.q: Why might a real organization deliberately put its gold layer in a Warehouse, even if bronze and silver live in a Lakehouse?
options: An analyst team comfortable with T-SQL can maintain the gold aggregation themselves using native INSERT/UPDATE support
Warehouses are required for any Delta table larger than 1000 rows
Gold layers cannot exist in a Lakehouse under any circumstances
This mixed pattern never actually happens in practice
questions.explain: This matches the same reasoning as the deciding-factor table earlier in the lesson — who's actually doing the querying.
